note: Current review queue refreshed for the five submitted links, two observed product categories, owner-supplied tracking-ID status, canonical reader-layer decision and the repository's disabled/unhosted measurement prototype. Recommendations are not owner decisions; account, product intent and runtime status remain unverified where stated.

states.do-now: Recommended for the first pass. Cheap, unblocked, and removes a visible defect.
states.do-next: Recommended, but it depends on a decision or a design pass.
states.blocked: Cannot be built until the named question is answered. The blocker is a policy gate, not a preference.
states.defer: Worth doing later. Doing it now costs more than it returns.
states.do-not-do: Proposed and rejected. The policy reason is recorded on the row.

columns_note: Priority P1/P2/P3 is sequencing, not importance. Effort S/M/L is a rough sizing against a single focused pass. Risk is the compliance or trust exposure if the item is done badly.

suggestions.title: Split the site into a reader surface and an evidence surface
suggestions.what: Keep the audit build, but make it reachable from one link labelled How we verify. Build a separate reader-facing surface that leads with the buying decision.

suggestions.title: Rename every navigation entry to a reader destination
suggestions.what: Replace process-named and session-named entries with Home, Reviews, Comparisons, Buying guides, How we verify. Four current entries are named after agent sessions.

suggestions.title: Move the audit counts out of the landing page hero
suggestions.what: An earlier draft used '0 of 3 prices verified' and a running flag count as headline statistics. The current root front page now presents five observed listing cards with volatile values omitted. Keep any future status counts in the evidence area and base them on the current five-link register.

suggestions.title: Adopt the design system in the brief
suggestions.what: Warm palette, named display and body type pairing, one accent reserved for action, hairline borders, no drop shadows except on the primary CTA.

suggestions.title: Publish How we verify as a real reader-facing page
suggestions.what: Sources, blanks, flags and what is deliberately unknown, written for a reader rather than for the build team.

suggestions.title: Question-led guide cluster for the current product scope
suggestions.what: Develop useful question-led guides for the five-link scope: keep three observed air-fryer listings and two meat-thermometer listings in separate category clusters until the owner confirms broader publication scope. Titles are hypotheses, not measured search demand.

suggestions.title: One canonical review page per product
suggestions.what: One product-intent record per submitted link. Keep intended ASIN/listing/date/source blank until confirmed; store the dated observed redirect target separately. This does not make the submitted short links invalid.

suggestions.title: Verdict above the fold plus a sticky comparison table
suggestions.what: One recommended sentence before any table; comparison table keeps its action column visible while scrolling.

suggestions.title: Product imagery through Amazon-served Program Content
suggestions.what: Use only an owner-approved, permitted source for volatile product fields. Account enrollment, API access and intended-product identity are not verified; current public pages leave price, rating and review fields out.

suggestions.title: Retire the duplicated category mirror page
suggestions.what: One canonical category page. A near-identical second target splits ranking and confuses readers.

suggestions.title: Deals or promotions page
suggestions.what: Rejected. Links to and mentions of a limited-time promotion must come down the moment the promotion ends, and nobody owns that step yet.

suggestions.title: Price tracking or price-drop alerts
suggestions.what: Rejected outright. The site must not have price tracking or price alerting functionality unless Amazon agrees otherwise.

suggestions.title: Brand and hero treatment for the landing page
suggestions.what: Keep a reader-first publication front page with two category entry points and the five observed listings clearly labelled as observations. No unsupported recommendation, winner, or assumed owner intent.

suggestions.title: Question-led editorial hub for two observed categories
suggestions.what: Maintain one guide hub for the twelve working title hypotheses in the current design brief. Keep air-fryer and thermometer questions in separate category clusters until scope is confirmed. Each published guide needs official sources, human review and explicit limits; titles do not prove popularity or search demand.
suggestions.why: A question-led hub can organize useful, source-backed explanations without implying measured demand or product testing. Use a dated query report for later topic prioritization when available.

suggestions.title: Human-review gate to remove the AI-slop feel
suggestions.what: A named reviewer signs off each page before publication against the anti-slop checklist.

suggestions.title: Comparison and buying-guide pages in marketing style
suggestions.what: Keep comparison and buyer-guide content limited to facts verified from the relevant official listing; distinguish listing claims from independent testing. Cover the current five observed links by two categories only after product intent is confirmed.

suggestions.title: Test one Associates Special Link per confirmed intended product before scaling
suggestions.what: The requester supplied shopnow047c-20, but it is not account-verified. In the enrolled workflow, create one Special Link for each confirmed intended product, verify the destination and report attribution, and only then scale. Keep supplied short links unchanged and unresolved.

suggestions.title: Trust section explaining how the site stays accurate
suggestions.what: A plain-language account of the sourcing rule and the deliberate blanks.

suggestions.title: SEO mechanics with honest meta descriptions
suggestions.what: Per-page titles and descriptions that state what the page actually contains.

suggestions.title: Trending-topics section anchored to official surfaces
suggestions.what: Any trend claim tied to a point-in-time read of an official Amazon surface, never to an inferred ranking.

suggestions.title: Keep the proposed measurement schema OFF until host review
suggestions.what: A five-event prototype proposal and collector script exist in the repository; the browser config is disabled and endpoint_url is empty. No collector runtime is hosted and no events are collected. Keep Amazon links direct and conversions report-sourced; review actual host/network logs, IP handling, retention and privacy notice before activation.

suggestions.title: Content cadence and a named editor before scaling
suggestions.what: Fix who publishes and how often before adding more articles.

suggestions.title: Choose one canonical buyer-facing page set before more route work
suggestions.what: Recommended default: root publication + /shop/ category/product pages + /guides/ question-led articles on the same host. Inventory unique content and inbound links in /site/, /read/, /marketing/ and /articles/ before any merge, archive, redirect or noindex change.
suggestions.risk: Medium: route changes can strand links or unique evidence.

suggestions.title: Review the proposed five events and host evidence before collecting anything
suggestions.what: The five event definitions in data/shop/measurement.json are a repository proposal, not owner-approved or live. The config is OFF with an empty endpoint URL; the collector script is unhosted. Do not enable until an actual runtime and its logging, IP handling, retention, access controls and applicable notice/consent requirements are reviewed.
suggestions.risk: High if a host collects identifiers or is described as privacy-safe without evidence.

suggestions.title: Adopt a human-reviewed cadence only after editor and query baseline are real
suggestions.what: A 14-day guide interval is a proposal, not a commitment. Name a real editor, record human sign-off, and use dated search/query evidence before making popularity claims or choosing a measured-demand topic. Keep the twelve supplied working titles labelled as hypotheses.
suggestions.risk: Medium if a fictional byline or unsupported demand claim is published.

questions.question: Is shopnow047c-20 the enrolled Associates ID for the intended marketplace, and does each intended product pass a Special Link report test?
questions.have: The repository records shopnow047c-20 as requester-supplied in data/shop/config.json; ownership, marketplace association and report attribution are not verified.
questions.missing: Account verification and one Associates-generated Special Link per owner-confirmed intended product, with the destination and report attribution checked.
questions.why: Blocks every conversion element on the site. Until it exists, no published link can earn.
questions.how: Verify the account/tag and marketplace; after intent confirmation, test one link per product in the enrolled Associates workflow before scaling. Keep submitted links as supplied and do not call them invalid.

questions.question: Are the five observed destination listings the five products the requester intended?
questions.have: Five dated short-link-to-listing observations are recorded; all five intended ASIN fields are blank.
questions.missing: The requester’s intended ASIN and official listing URL for each of the five submitted links.
questions.why: Product recommendations, comparisons and CTA destinations depend on intent; a redirect only records where a link opened.
questions.how: Ask the requester to confirm each intended listing, then record the official URL, date and source separately from the observed redirect. Do not label the submitted short links invalid.

questions.question: Which Amazon marketplace is the site for?
questions.have: All five dated observed destinations are Amazon.com pages. This does not establish the intended audience, target country, currency or Associates marketplace.
questions.missing: The owner’s chosen audience and marketplace, and a matching enrolled account.
questions.why: Determines link format, commission schedule and which rate table applies.
questions.how: Obtain the owner’s choice and verify the account marketplace in Associates Central; do not infer it from the observed Amazon.com destination or the requester’s location.

questions.question: Is the Associates account enrolled, and does it meet the API prerequisites?
questions.have: Creators API is the documented successor to PA-API 5, and it lists prerequisites including qualifying sales in a recent period.
questions.missing: The account's actual standing. This session did not re-read the prerequisites page and marks it as not re-read today.
questions.why: Gates price, availability, rating and review display, which gates the comparison table.
questions.how: Check standing in the Associates dashboard and read the Creators API prerequisites page directly.

questions.question: Who reviews and publishes content, and how often?
questions.have: No real human reviewer is named in the current records; the existing generated desk/byline label is not treated as a person. A 14-day interval is only a proposal.
questions.missing: A real editor/reviewer, their authority, review time and an owner-approved cadence.
questions.why: The human-review gate is the only durable defence against the generated-content feel.
questions.how: Assign an owner and a cadence before any article is published.

questions.question: Have any of the five products been used or tested first-hand?
questions.have: The repository contains listing observations and no first-hand test record for any of the five products.
questions.missing: Whether anyone will obtain/test the five products and, if so, the reviewer, method, dates and recorded results.
questions.why: Decides whether the site can publish reviews or only analyses of published information, and the FTC expects the difference to be honest.
questions.how: If testing occurs, record the actual reviewer, units, dates, protocol and observations; otherwise keep statements to source-backed listing facts and explicit limits.

questions.question: What brand direction should the marketing site use?
questions.have: The current identity is a default UI blue and the system font stack.
questions.missing: A name, palette and voice decision.
questions.why: Blocks design work; a palette cannot be chosen by a build script.
questions.how: Owner decision against the design system in the brief.

questions.question: What analytics/reporting route is wanted, and where can a runtime be hosted with verified logging and retention?
questions.have: The repository includes five proposed event definitions and an unhosted collector prototype; enabled=false, endpoint_url empty, ledger empty. GitHub Pages is static and its docs state visitor IPs are logged.
questions.missing: Owner approval/revision of the proposal; a runtime host; actual network/access logging, IP handling, retention, controls, applicable notice/consent review and authorized Associates reports.
questions.why: A local collector script is not a deployed service. No site events or Amazon conversion data are evidenced, and “privacy-preserving” cannot be claimed without host evidence.
questions.how: Keep collection OFF. Review the proposed schema and host’s official docs; inspect actual staging logs/retention before activation. Use authorized Associates reports for orders, not a browser conversion event.

questions.question: What budget and tooling exist for keyword and topic research?
questions.have: No Search Console query export or measured reader-query dataset is recorded; the current titles are editorial hypotheses.
questions.why: Sets how the twelve articles are sequenced.
questions.how: Choose a research tool for prioritisation only, keeping its numbers out of published claims.

questions.question: Should the disclosure placement be reviewed by counsel before launch?
questions.have: The Operating Agreement requires the disclosure clearly and prominently, and the FTC expects it where the endorsement appears.
questions.missing: A sign-off that the chosen placement satisfies both.
questions.why: Disclosure placement is the most common enforcement trigger in affiliate publishing.
questions.how: Have the template reviewed once, then reuse the pattern.

questions.question: Which reader-facing page set is canonical, and how should overlapping pages be handled?
questions.have: The current tree has root, /shop/ and /guides/ reader pages plus overlapping /site/, /read/, /marketing/ and /articles/ layers. Root + shop + guides is a recommendation, not an owner choice.
questions.missing: The accepted canonical page set, final publisher name, and a map of unique content and inbound links before routes change.
questions.why: A clear reader route is needed, but unreviewed consolidation could strand inbound links or lose unique evidence.
questions.how: Review the proposed root + /shop/ + /guides/ default, inventory unique content/links, and record an owner decision before any redirect/archive/noindex.

questions.question: Does the evidence surface stay public?
questions.have: The audit build and the source register are public today and are the most unusual asset on the site.
questions.missing: A decision on whether it is a marketing asset or internal documentation.
questions.why: If public it is a differentiator and a link magnet; if internal it should not be in the reader nav at all.
questions.how: Decide, then either promote it to How we verify or remove it from the reader navigation.

questions.question: Should the three air-fryer and two meat-thermometer listings share one publication, and what category structure should readers see?
questions.have: The dated shop register groups three observed listings as air fryers and two as meat thermometers; this is not owner-confirmed niche scope.
questions.missing: Whether the owner intends one broader kitchen publication or distinct niche sites/category clusters.
questions.why: The five observed listings are split across two categories (three air fryers and two meat thermometers); the listing count alone does not establish owner intent or reader demand. Expanding either content cluster also requires sourcing capacity.
questions.how: Keep the two categories distinct pending owner decision. Use the route/content inventory to choose the reader structure; do not infer audience or demand from the links.

questions.question: Who owns removing expired promotions?
questions.have: Links to and mentions of a limited-time promotion must be removed as soon as the promotion ends on Amazon.
questions.why: Without an owner, a deals page becomes a standing compliance breach.
questions.how: Name an owner, or keep the deals page off the roadmap entirely.

questions.question: What publisher name will the site use?
questions.have: Amazon marks may not appear in the domain, subdomain, Associates tag or social handles.
questions.why: Blocks brand work and is expensive to change later, because every link carries the tag.
questions.how: Choose a name that contains no Amazon mark before the tag is issued.

relationship_note: This audit-side review console sits beside the reader publication, shop decisions and browser-local Decision Center. Recommended default: root + /shop/ + /guides/ on one host; group evidence/decision pages under one nav/footer item. This remains a proposal until the owner chooses it and unique content/inbound links are mapped. The Choice UI stores only in the current browser; it does not record an owner decision.
